explanation: W = 1.4885 GeV is only ~2.4 MeV above the eta-p production threshold (1.4861 GeV) and is inside the 10 MeV band the exclurad preflight check flags as WARN: the eta-MAID lookup table (maid07-PPpi.tbl, which despite its filename holds EtaMAID-2023 multipoles) is known to make the integrator hang indefinitely or exit with no 'tai:' line (silent N/A) at points this close to threshold. Q2 = 0.5 GeV^2 and cos(theta*) = 0.2 are both fine (table covers W in [1.4856, 6.0] GeV and Q2 in [0.0, 5.0] GeV^2; cos(theta*) is far from the +/-1 poles), and vcut = 0.166 GeV^2 (channel default) passed. I generated the input file anyway since the point is not physically forbidden, but you should run it as a smoke test with a timeout before trusting or batching it, since it may hang or come back with no result. Settings used: beam = 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K, the campaign the validated eta reference data came from -- 10.6 GeV RG-A and 10.2 GeV RG-B are also valid but give different radiative corrections), rc_mode = 0 (full O(alpha), the only mode used for validated results), vcut = 0.166 GeV^2 (channel default).
